verdict.rationale: Lithic ships an official MCP server that lets AI assistants in editors (Cursor, Claude Code, Copilot) search docs, inspect schemas, generate integration code, and execute live API requests via natural language, and a blog post demonstrates agentic workflows like creating cards and configuring auth rules through this interface. However, this is developer-tool-mediated natural language (via MCP in a coding assistant), not a native conversational interface within Lithic's own product, and there's no independent/hands-on corroboration of reliability. missing for 10: independent/third-party validation of the MCP server's natural-language command accuracy, evidence of a first-party conversational/chat interface outside of editor-based MCP tooling.
